comment: TOML-IDENTITY. Every symbol's NAME is its full dotted path from the document root, authored from the TOML v1.0.0 key grammar BEFORE observing output. Three facts are load-bearing here. (1) A key before any header belongs to the IMPLICIT ROOT table, so its owner is the module. (2) A quoted key is ONE segment even when it contains a dot — `a.b` and `"a.b"` are different keys and a name that cannot be read back is not an identity, so the ambiguous one keeps TOML's own quotes. Three spellings appear side by side to prove they stay distinct: `plain.dotted`, `"dotted.literal"` and `"dotted.literal".child`. (3) IMPLIED PARENTS ARE RECORDED, NOT MATERIALISED: `[workspace.lints.rust]` implies `workspace` and `workspace.lints`, and the file never declares either, so they appear in metadata and NOT as symbols. Fabricating them would be a guess dressed as a fact.

expectSymbols.name: identity-and-paths
expectSymbols.comment: the FILE is the module, named from its stem — never from the filename, so `Cargo.toml` is `Cargo`

expectSymbols.name: root_key
expectSymbols.comment: a key before any header belongs to the implicit root table, so its owner is the module

expectSymbols.name: package."dotted.literal"
expectSymbols.comment: a quoted key is ONE segment; the quotes are what make it readable back, and without them it would be indistinguishable from `package.plain.dotted`

expectSymbols.name: package.plain.dotted
expectSymbols.comment: bare dotted: three real nested tables

expectSymbols.name: package."dotted.literal".child
expectSymbols.comment: a quoted segment followed by a bare one — the third distinct spelling of the same shape

expectSymbols.name: workspace.lints.rust
expectSymbols.comment: the header's own path is the name; the two tables it IMPLIES are recorded here and are not published as symbols

expectSymbols.name: workspace.lints.rust.unsafe_code
expectSymbols.comment: a key's name is prefixed by its table's ALLOCATED name, so the edge from the table resolves

forbidSymbols.name: workspace
forbidSymbols.comment: IMPLIED PARENTS ARE RECORDED, NOT MATERIALISED. The file never declares `[workspace]`, so no symbol is invented for it — a fabricated table is a guess dressed as a fact.

forbidSymbols.name: workspace.lints
forbidSymbols.comment: same: implied by the header, never written, so never a symbol

forbidSymbols.name: package.dotted.literal
forbidSymbols.comment: the UNQUOTED spelling of a key that was written quoted. If this name were published, `plain.dotted` and `"dotted.literal"` would be one identity and the second would silently shadow the first.

expectRelationships.comment: the edge names the table that EXISTS; the implied parents are metadata, not nodes

forbidRelationships.comment: TOML DEFINES NO REFERENCE MECHANISM — no include, no import, no link. A path-shaped string like `src/main.rs` is a STRING, and treating such strings as dependencies would import ecosystem knowledge (which keys are paths in which tool) into a format that has none. So there is no `uses`, and the graph is `contains` only.
same: nothing in a TOML document is fetched or imported.
